label: Ayer's 1936 test is trivial: in any TRUTH_CONDITIONAL_LANGUAGE_4, a…, by Constructive-proof
meaning: From no premises, for every truth-conditional language: take the further premise P = (not-s or o) for an observation statement o. Then s with P entails o. If P alone entailed o, then not-s would entail o (not-s entails P). So whenever not-s does not entail o, s passes Ayer's 1936 test.
